players.outlook: Christian Watson will look to build off a career day as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Watson put together a prolific performance in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, bringing in seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown. The wideout now holds a career-high receiving line of 49-879-7 on 74 targets. He'll face a Minnesota secondary that he tore up with 6 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns against in Week 1.

Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in Week 10 as the Packers take on the Vikings. Jacobs hurt his finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, and he's now set to undergo surgery, which will keep him out for a maximum of three weeks. The veteran ball carrier has now recorded 36 rushes for 80 yards and a touchdown, with 11 catches for 68 yards and two touchdowns as well. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong, and banged-up Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd will be Green Bay's available running backs against a tough Minnesota defense.

news.text: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.. Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. players.outlook: Caleb Douglas continues to make big plays on increased chances ahead of the the Dolphins' Week 11 game against the Bills. Douglas notched eight targets for the second-straight game in Week 10, reaching 70 yards for the third time in four outings. While new quarterback Kyle McCord threw 32 passes to 11 different teammates in his debut, Douglas remained the steady top option. Buffalo allows just 7.3 yards per target, the eighth-lowest in the league, but with Miami likely to be throwing from behind often, Douglas can be a preferred option.

news.text: Douglas (shoulder) is expected to play Sunday against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.. Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

players.outlook: Puka Nacua is expected to miss the Rams' Week 10 clash against the Cardinals and several weeks beyond that. Nacua suffered a knee injury in this past Sunday's win over Washington and is likely to be placed on IR. Davante Adams (hamstring) remains on IR, so the Rams' WR corps will be led by the likes of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington.

news.text: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.. Given that timetable, Nacua -- who is already on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In his continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12, following the team's bye.

players.outlook: Brock Bowers played just 11 offensive snaps in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury, catching both his targets for 18 yards. The star tight end's injury isn't thought to be too serious, but he could miss at least a game or two, potentially opening the door for Michael Mayer to have a bigger role. If Bowers is able to suit up in Week 11 and continue building chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, he'll be taking on a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

news.text: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.. Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end doesn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers already has cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

players.outlook: Trey McBride is set to work with rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the second time when the Cardinals travel to Kansas City for a Week 11 clash. McBride had his season-opening streak of logging at least seven receptions snapped this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams, when he managed a quiet 5-37-0 receiving line on five targets. Nonetheless, every part of his line (catches, receiving yardage and targets) led the Cardinals in a game during which Beck struggled mightily to move the ball. There could be an opportunity for McBride to post better numbers against Kansas City, who have given up the

Ryan Flournoy has scored in three of the last five contests for the Cowboys. Flournoy has caught at least two passes in every game this season, and has drawn at least four targets in all but one contest. In Week 11, Flournoy has a tasty matchup against the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

Bucky Irving will likely remain the focal points of the Buccaneers' offense during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Irving has carried Tampa Bay's offense throughout the season, ranking sixth in the NFL in touches per game (21.0) and 10th in total yards per game (103.4). However, head coach Todd Bowles said that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following the team's Week 10 bye, suggesting he could see less work going forward. Additionally, Irving may struggle in Week 11 against a Lions defense that's held opposing running backs in check this season, allowing just 1

Mike Evans reportedly has a chance to return from an Achilles injury for San Francisco's Week 11 tilt against the Vikings. Evans has missed the 49ers' past three games while dealing with right Achilles tendinitis. San Francisco recently acquired veteran Keenan Allen to bolster the wideout corps, and Deebo Samuel returned in Week 10 from a multi-game absence caused by a hamstring injury, but Evans' ability to get back on the field would still be a big boost given his chemistry with QB Brock Purdy this season. The 49ers can use all the help they can get on Sunday Night Football, as Minnesota has

news.text: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.. Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

players.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11. His hot streak continued during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, as he threw for 409 yards with four TDs and no INTs while rushing once for eight yards. Over his last five outings, all Bengals wins, Burrow has compiled 1,624 passing yards with a 20:3 TD:INT ratio, while adding 47 rushing yards and another two scores. The NFL's leading passer in terms of TDs (27) will aim to keep rolling versus the Commanders' 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to opposing QBs.

Jonah Coleman captured the No. 1 job in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the team's last two games, the rookie running back amassed 192 scrimmage yards and two rushing TDs, with his yardage split almost equally between the ground and the air. Coleman's usage as a pass catcher could decline once RJ Harvey gets healthy in a couple of weeks, but he's clearly surpassed J.K. Dobbins as the preferred ball carrier in all situations, including at the goal line. Coleman will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Dak Prescott tied a career high with five touchdown passes last game for Dallas. Unfortunately, the Cowboys defense could not stop a nosebleed, as they fell by a staggering score of 46-40 to the 49ers. Dak also threw for a season-high 343 yards, notching his second-straight 300-yard output overall. Dak has tossed multiple touchdowns in three of the last four contests. In Week 11, Dak will look to keep rolling against a suspect Tennessee pass defense. The Titans are allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep up his dominance as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Gibbs had another monster performance in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, totaling 252 yards off 29 touches and tacking on two rushing touchdowns. The superstar has now amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine showings. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

Denzel Boston and the Browns welcome the 3-5 Texans to town in Week 10. He corralled six of seven targets for 98 yards during Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss in Week 9. Boston just missed the 100-yard mark but established a new career high in receiving yards, pacing his team in receptions, yardage, and targets. He showed great rapport with Shedeur Sanders, who earned his first start of the season, but Deshaun Watson (concussion) is likely to return from a one-game absence to face his former team. Boston will look to build upon this effort against a Houston defense allowing the third-most fanta

Blake Corum continues to get a hefty share of work out of the Rams' backfield heading into a Week 10 visit to Arizona. Corum led Los Angeles with 58 rushing yards and scored a touchdown on 11 carries in a Week 9 win against Washington. Though he remains marginally behind Kyren Williams in the Rams' backfield, Corum has logged double-digit carries in three straight games and has scored in each of those contests. There could be an opportunity for both Corum and Williams to succeed against a Cardinals defense that is giving up 99.6 rushing yards per game to RBs, ranking 19th in the league.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that

Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the receiver's former team when the Colts come to town in Week 5. He hauled in two of four targets for 15 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, giving him a 7-89-0 receiving line on 12 targets across three contests. It's been a slow start for Pittman in his debut season for the Steelers, but Week 5 offers a shot at some payback against the team that drafted him in 2020. Indianapolis' defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs, a matchup that could help Pittman's chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

news.text: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.. After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

players.outlook: CeeDee Lamb continues to pile up statistics for the Dallas Cowboys. Lamb found the end zone for the second-straight game and eighth time overall in 2026 in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Lamb finished with seven catches for 72 yards and the score. Lamb has drawn double-digit targets in five-straight contests, a trend that should continue in Week 11 versus the Titans. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is dead last in the NFL.

Javonte Williams was held out of the end zone for the second time in three games for the Cowboys. Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Williams was also held under 65 yards rushing for the second time in three contests. However, his usage remains high, as he has received double-digit carries in every game in 2026. In Week 11, Williams will face a Titans squad that has been lackluster against the run. Tennessee is allowing 124 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 22nd in the league.

Jayden Daniels tossed three touchdown passes last game for the Commanders. He also threw his first two interceptions of the season in the thrilling 24-21 win over the Giants. Daniels has thrown for at least 215 yards in four-straight contests. He may be more successful with his legs than with his arm in Week 11 versus the Bengals, though. Cincinnati is allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. By contrast, Cincy is surrendering 123.9 rushing yards per clash, which is 21st in the league.

Lamar Jackson is heading to the IR after taking just one snap for the Ravens in Week 9. He missed the prior three contests with a high-ankle injury, and now thumb surgery could end his season. Tyler Huntley took over, but he had to exit with a toe injury, forcing emergency third-string QB Joe Fagnano into action. More will be known about Jackson's status after he goes under a very small knife.

news.text: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.. Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entr

players.outlook: Josh Downs made an immediate difference in his Kansas City debut, catching four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Falcons despite running just eight routes and playing only 10 snaps. Picked up from the Colts at the trade deadline, Downs' efficiency on a limited workload bodes well, but he'll still be the No. 2 wide receiver behind Rashee Rice, with Travis Kelce and the team's running backs also factoring significantly into the passing game. Downs will try to build on this performance in Week 11 against a Cardinals secondary that ranks 17th in fantasy points

Jason Myers will hope for more kicking opportunities when Seattle faces Las Vegas in Week 10. Myers made his lone field goal and both his extra-point tries in Week 9 against Arizona as the Seahawks scored fewer than 21 points for the fourth straight week. The veteran kicker has been good when called upon this season, though, making 16 of 18 FG tries through nine games. He could be more active against the Raiders, who are giving up a league-worst 29.8 points per game.

Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

Bhayshul Tuten has scored six times during his current four-game TD streak, and he has mustered at least 87 scrimmage yards in seven of Jacksonville's nine games this season. The second-year stud has crept into fantasy RB1 territory ahead of Jacksonville's Week 11 road game against the Giants, who have allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs but also three receiving TDs to the position through nine games. Tuten has five rushing TDs and three receiving scores this season while notching at least 12 carries in every game and two-plus receptions in all but two outings. His well-rounded skill set allo

news.text: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation -- or lack thereof -- in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

players.outlook: Omar Cooper is questionable to suit up for the Jets against the Chargers in Week 11 due to an ankle injury. Cooper managed just one snap in Week 10 as the same ankle that cost him four weeks earlier in the season flared up, resulting in his second game in three weeks without a catch. Pairing that with quarterback uncertainty, with Geno Smith also dealing with an ankle injury, Cooper profiles as a volatile, deep option against a secondary that's allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing receivers.

news.text: Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Cooper (ankle/hip) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.. Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

players.outlook: The Texans led the league with 13 weeks as a top-10 scoring defense, allowed the fewest yards and second-fewest points and totaled the third-most interceptions and seventh-most sacks, last season. Edge rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter and cornerback Derek Stingley were among five Pro Bowlers from their roster, which largely returns the same personnel for 2026. The Texans make a compelling case to be the first D/ST picked, with one caveat: Their tricky September schedule includes the Bills (Week 1), Bengals (2) and Cowboys (4) and will probably demand fantasy managers seek fill-ins for

Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his situation as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Mason led Minnesota's backfield with 16 carries for 59 yards in a Week 10 win over the Packers, but teammate Aaron Jones punched in the only touchdown from the pair. Mason has yet to record a score in four outings since returning from a thumb injury, but he's put together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry. He'll face a San Francisco defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

Brandon Aubrey connected on two field goals and two extra points for the Cowboys in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Aubrey did miss an extra point, his second of the season. However, both of Aubrey's field goals came from 50-plus yards out, giving him five such field goals on the season to date. In Week 11, Dallas will face a bumbling Titans squad. Tennessee is allowing 26.6 points per contest, which is 27th in the league.

Chris Rodriguez remains a touchdown dependent deep league flex option for Week 11, though his chances of cashing in aren't great against a Giants defense that has allowed just four rushing TDs to RBs all season. Rodriguez had a season low five yards in Jacksonville's Week 10 win over the Titans. He has scored on the ground in four of Jacksonville's nine games while rushing for at least 55 yards twice, but Rodriguez remains a non-factor as a receiver, with just four catches for 36 yards all season. Bhayshul Tuten remains the clear No. 1 RB for the Jaguars.

news.text: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

players.outlook: Braelon Allen remains second fiddle to Breece Hall ahead of the Jets' Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. In two games since Hall's return, Allen has 16 carries compared to Hall's 26. Hall has also caught seven passes to Allen's three. Despite being more efficient than Hall, Allen's role appears clear in a matchup against a defense that's allowing a modest 4.0 yards per carry, likely rendering Allen to flex territory.

DJ Moore will seek more big plays in Week 11 when the Bills face the Dolphins. Moore is averaging 16.3 yards per catch, the second-highest mark of his nine-year career, and gets an inviting matchup with a secondary that's allowing 9.3 yards per target to wideouts, the sixth-highest mark league-wide. Moore will need those big yardage chances as Buffalo threw only 21 times in Week 10 while blowing out the Jets, and a similar game script is likely against Miami.

Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top pass catcher during the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. London has cooled down after a terrific stretch of games from Weeks 3 through 5, averaging just 4.3 receptions and 52.8 receiving yards per game over Atlanta's last four contests. He's also averaging just 7.6 targets per game this season, his lowest mark since 2023, so it appears the Falcons are struggling to get him involved. Additionally, London is in for a difficult Week 10 matchup against a Chiefs secondary that's allowed just 23.5 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts thi

Kenneth Walker didn't suit up for Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons due to a minor groin injury. In his place, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. Walker is expected back in Week 11 against Arizona, but Johnson's performance could lead to more volume for the team's backup RB as the focus shifts toward making sure Walker still has something left for the playoffs, given KC's 7-2 record. Assuming Walker is cleared to return, he'll be facing a Cardinals defense that's tied for 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

news.text: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday.. Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

players.outlook: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Kraft didn't get to join in on any of the fun of Green Bay's offensive explosion in Week 9 over the Patriots, as he brought in just one of his three targets for one yard and rushed the ball twice for eight yards. He's now posted a 36-351-3 receiving line across the first nine games of the campaign. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he logged three catches for 65 yards against in Week 1.

DeVonta Smith could return from a hamstring issue for the Eagles following their bye. Smith has missed five of the last six games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of Dontayvion Wicks, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

Woody Marks entered concussion protocol during Houston's Week 10 loss to the the Browns. He isn't expected to be cleared in time to face the Colts on Thursday Night Football in Week 11. David Montgomery (groin) would likely assume the lead role in Houston's backfield if he gains clearance for his first action since Week 5. Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale are Houston's other options at RB.

news.text: Marks (concussion) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Colts.. After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns, Marks will be sidelined for the first time this season after he was unable to practice in any capacity on a short week. The second-year player had been operating as the Texans' clear lead back over the past four contests, but for at least one week, those duties are expected to fall to David Montgomery (groin), who has been cleared to return to action following a four-game absence. Once Marks clears the protocol, he could be form a timeshare with Montgomery.

players.outlook: Omarion Hampton is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, topping 100 rushing yards for the first time and scoring his first touchdown since Week 4. It was a big step toward Hampton regaining the clear No. 1 job in the backfield, as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combined for just seven touches and 18 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 11 against a Jets defense that's tied for 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Emeka Egbuka is expected to lead the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Egbuka has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 season, catching 31 of 54 targets for 278 yards and two touchdowns in seven games. Despite this poor start, he ranks first on the Buccaneers in receiving yards, receptions, targets and touchdowns this year, suggesting more fantasy production is imminent. Egbuka could thrive against the Lions' secondary in Week 11, as they have allowed 32.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wide receiver groups this season.

Corey Kiner could be in line for a significant role for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions, with both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) uncertain to play. While Detroit is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing backs, volume remains king, and Kiner could serve as the No. 1 RB for Week 10 in Munich. Kiner figures to be a popular play in what could be a high-scoring game, despite Detroit allowing just 3.9 yards per carry.

Brock Purdy is coming off one of the best performances of his career as the 49ers prepare to host Minnesota in Week 11. Purdy threw for a career-best 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. The star quarterback now ranks second among QBs with at least 100 pass attempts in QB rating (115.2) and has posted an impressive 20:5 TD:INT. However, Purdy faces a tough test in the Vikings, who lead the NFL with 37 sacks and have allowed only six passing touchdowns while recording 10 interceptions.

Trey Smack will aim to stay on track as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. After a less-than-optimal start to the season, Smack reeled it in against the Patriots in Week 9, nailing all three field-goal attempts and four PATs. The rookie kicker has still made just five of his last nine field-goal tries, so he'll need to stay accurate against a Minnesota defense that he made three field goals against in Week 1.

Sam LaPorta will aim to get back on track as the Lions return home against the Patriots in Week 11. LaPorta has had an extremely dry stretch ever since Detroit's bye week, failing to reach 40 yards in four straight games. The starting tight end has now recorded 36 receptions for 415 yards and three touchdowns, with most of his volume coming from the first five outings of the season. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 23rd in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

Zach Charbonnet seems to be emerging as Seattle's No. 1 running back heading into a Week 10 tilt against the Raiders. In his second game back from ACL surgery, Charbonnet led the Seahawks with 16 carries and 77 receiving yards against Arizona this past Sunday while adding one catch for nine yards. Rookie Jadarian Price still managed 13 touches, so Charbonnet doesn't seem likely to have the backfield all to himself. Both tailbacks could thrive against a Las Vegas defense that has allowed a league-worst 5.21 yards per carry to running backs.

Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 11 clash versus Minnesota having been largely utilized for extra points thanks to San Francisco's highly efficient offense. Pineiro has gone just 8-for-11 on FG tries this season but leads the NFL with 35 PAT tries, of which he's made 31. That's largely because the 49ers have been extremely effective at getting into the end zone, and they are scoring 31.2 points per game -- second in the NFL. Something may have to give against the Vikings, who are allowing the fewest points per game (14.0) in the league.

Jalen Coker will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Panthers' Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. After catching 16 of 18 targets for 204 yards and two touchdowns across Carolina's first two games this season, Coker has managed just 15 receptions on 35 targets for 189 yards and one touchdown over his last six contests. He remains second on the team in receptions (31), targets (53) and receiving yards (393) but likely can't be trusted after four consecutive performances of less than 10.0 fantasy points. However, Coker is in for a favorable Week 11 matchup against a Baltimore sec

Jameson Williams will remain a flashy option in Detroit's offense heading into Week 11 against the Buccaneers. Williams didn't benefit, like some of his teammates, from an offensive explosion in a Week 10 win over New England, but he still hauled in four of seven targets for 50 yards. The speedy wideout has now logged 32 catches for 518 yards and five touchdowns so far this season. He'll take on a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

Rachaad White is averaging at least four yards per carry over his last three games with the Commanders. Though White is technically the starting running back, he has only had double-digit carries twice this season. Moreover, Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return soon from Injured Reserve. For now, though, White remains the top dog in the backfield heading into a Week 11 clash with the Bengals. Cincy has been better against the pass than the run in 2026. The Bengals are allowing 123.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.

Courtland Sutton caught a season-high five passes in the Broncos' last game before their Week 10 bye, turning one of the receptions into his second touchdown of the season. The veteran wide receiver's target volume increased after Jaylen Waddle left the contest early due to a concussion. He has yet to reach 50 receiving yards or see double-digit targets in any game this year as the No. 2 option in a sluggish passing game. Sutton will attempt to contribute in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

A lack of opportunities could keep the Bills' Dalton Kincaid from exploiting the Dolphins' defense in Week 11. He had just three targets for the second straight game in Week 10, and his snap share has declined in each of the last three games since Buffalo's Week 7 bye, reaching a season-low 46% in Week 10. Buffalo has been a run-heavy offense, often leaving Kincaid off the field in favor of more traditional blocking tight ends. With declining snaps, he will be left with too few chances to beat a defense that's allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

news.text: Kincaid (thumb) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.. With Kincaid now having missed the open portion of practice on consecutive days, his status will remain worth tracking heading into Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If the tight end is unavailable or limited, Buffalo could have to lean more on DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in the middle of the field, while Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu would handle tight-end duties.

players.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a rare quiet game with Seattle's Week 10 matchup in Las Vegas on tap. The All-Pro wideout logged a season-low 51 yards on seven catches this past Sunday against Arizona, though he still drew a healthy 10 targets. Drew Lock (oblique) started at quarterback for the Seahawks in that contest and is expected to do so again in Week 10, as Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib) is likely to remain sidelined. Regardless, Smith-Njigba could feast against a Raiders defense that ranks 26th in the league with 23.6 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Drake Maye appears poised for a busy outing in Week 10 when the Patriots face the Lions. Maye has tossed multiple touchdown passes in six straight outings (17 total), three times going for 299 yards or more, and could be asked to throw at a high rate with running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson uncertain to suit up. Pair that with a matchup against a Lions secondary that's allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, and Maye could provide elite numbers in Week 10's Sunday morning affair in Germany.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

Devin Singletary played just five snaps last game for the Giants. With Cam Skattebo healthy, Singletary was left largely riding the pine, a spot he will likely continue to occupy in Week 11 versus the Jags. The matchup versus Jacksonville is also far from ideal. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.

Davante Adams was placed on Injured Reserve due to a ruptured left hamstring in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals and is expected to be sidelined until after the Rams' Week 11 bye in a best-case scenario. With Adams out, names such as Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell should be in line for more targets, while established threats in the passing game like Puka Nacua, Tyler Higbee and Kyren Williams will also be in line for an uptick in numbers. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

players.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens take to the road in Week 11 to battle the 4-5 Panthers. In Baltimore's Week 10 loss, he rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 10 yards. Henry was able to salvage an otherwise miserable outing with two scores, the 32-year-old's ninth and tenth rushing TDs on the season. The Ravens attempted 49 passes with Jacoby Brissett making his team debut under center. Breece Hall brings steady volume into a somewhat challenging matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Hall has amassed at least 11 carries in both games since returning from injury while adding seven receptions, tallying 195 total yards though not reaching the end zone and continuing to share reps with Braelon Allen. The Chargers are allowing the 10th most fantasy points per game to opposing backs, but just 4.0 yards per carry and an even lower 3.9 yards per reception. Hall remains a lineup mainstay and could surge in the receiving game if Cade Klubnik is forced into action over Gen

Alvin Kamara will remain one of the Saints' top running backs in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Kamara was limited to just five touches while Travis Etienne returned from injury in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers. However, Kamara scored two touchdowns on those touches and appeared to be operating as New Orleans' top red-zone RB. With Kamara, Etienne and Audric Estime all playing roles in the Saints' backfield, it may be hard to trust any of them going forward. Kamara could take advantage of a Chicago defense that's allowed 7.3 yards per target and two receiving touchdowns to opposing

Travis Kelce is coming off his least productive game of the season, catching both his targets for 30 yards in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons. The veteran tight end hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 3, and he hasn't hauled in more than five passes or 72 receiving yards since Week 2, but his role as Patrick Mahomes' most reliable security blanket gives him a fairly secure floor. Kelce will look to make a bigger contribution in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. His recent downturn has knocked Shrader out of first place in field goals made and attempted, though he's still top-three in both categories thanks to a torrid start that has the Colts' kicker at 23-for-25 through 10 games. That strong start included a 4-for-4 Week 3 performance against the Texans, whom Shrader will face again in Week 11. The Colts' offense has been depleted by a few trades and will likely struggle to generate consistent kicking opportunities moving forward, but Shrader is viable in Week 11 s

Aaron Jones will look to build off a solid showing as the Vikings travel to San Francisco in Week 11. Jones did well against his former squad in Week 10, logging 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, along with catching one pass for eight yards. The veteran remains in a timeshare with Jordan Mason, but he still holds some value moving forward. The 49ers have ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to RBs this campaign.

Matthew Golden will look to keep his tear rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Golden logged a career-best 164 yards on 10 catches and found the end zone in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. The second-year breakout receiver also caught every one of his targets in the win, which was a huge improvement from some drop-heavy games this season. He'll face a Minnesota defense that he caught six passes for 95 yards against in Week 1.

Deebo Samuel will look to build on his best performance of the season when the 49ers  host the Vikings in Week 11. Samuel compiled 109 total yards and two touchdowns this past Sunday in a win over Dallas, with most of that yardage coming on a 70-yard rushing score. It was Samuel's first game if five weeks, as he had been sidelined due to a hamstring injury. His versatility could come in handy against a Vikings defense that is tied for the third-fewest receiving TDs (five) allowed to wideouts this season.

Kyle Monangai will look to make a return as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Monangai has sat out five straight games as he works back from a turf-toe injury. The second-year ball carrier's status is very likely correlated with his ability to practice, so this week should reveal his expected return timeline. He accrued 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns off 60 carries in the first four games of the season. If he returns, Monangai will face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs this season.

Zay Flowers and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the Panthers in Week 11. He corralled six of seven targets for 74 yards but lost a key fumble during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. Flowers turned it over with 2:11 remaining, ultimately ending his team's chance to tie or take the lead. On a brighter note, Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, meaning Flowers should have no shortage of opportunities to make up for the costly mistake versus Carolina's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (31.5) to WRs.

Saquon Barkley did find the end zone last game for the Eagles, but was otherwise bottled up. Barkley managed just 22 yards on the ground along with the score in the 19-11 loss to the Giants before the bye. With third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, Saquon will likely see a stacked box in Week 11 versus the Steelers. Pittsburgh has been stellar in defending the run in 2026 as well, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league. Likewise, Pittsburgh has yielded just five rushing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.

Jake Ferguson left the last game for Dallas due to an ankle injury. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus Indianapolis. Ferguson has failed to register a single catch in each of the last two contests. Brevyn Spann-Ford could see additional looks if Ferguson is sidelined. Spann-Ford snagged five passes for 31 yards following Ferguson's departure. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

news.text: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.. Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

players.outlook: In Week 11, Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to snap a five-game losing streak when they visit the 4-5 Panthers. He's coming off easily his best outing of the season in Week 10's loss, as he caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards while leading the team in receptions and yardage. Andrews established new season highs in each receiving category with the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett making his first start for Baltimore. Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards, and if that trend continues for the Ravens' offense, Andrews could be primed for a much larger role moving forward.

Will Shipley could return from a foot injury next game for the Eagles. Shipley has not played since Week 5 but has a chance to see the field in Week 11 versus the Steelers. However, with third-string quarterback Joe Milton under center, and Saquon Barkley healthy, Shipley's workload could be extremely limited. Pittsburgh has also been stellar in defending the run in 2026, allowing just 83.2 yards per tilt on the ground, which is third in the league.

news.text: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.. Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

players.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals visit Washington on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He brought in five of six targets for 66 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, extending the team's win streak to five games. Higgins' consecutive outings with a TD snapped, however, as he failed to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5. Head coach Zac Taylor relayed Higgins' workload was being managed toward the end of the win over Pittsburgh, so keep an eye on his status in practice during Week 11 prep.

Travis Etienne will look to make a larger impact as the Saints' take on the Bears in Week 11. Etienne was relatively ineffective in his return from injury during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, logging 11 touches for 34 yards. Despite Etienne serving as New Orleans' top running back, Audric Estime took most of the short-yardage work, and Alvin Kamara operated as the team's top red-zone back, scoring two touchdowns. Jordan Love will look to keep his MVP campaign rolling as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Love was on fire again in a Week 9 win over the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three passing touchdowns and a 13-yard rushing score. Green Bay's signal caller has now dished out two or more touchdowns and passed for 270 or more yards in each of his last three outings. He'll rematch a Vikings defense that he threw for 387 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against in a Week 1 loss.

Despite the lack of efficiency, Miller has led New Orleans' backfield in carries three consecutive games, which bodes well for his outlook while Etienne remains out. Miller could find success against the Browns' defense in Week 9, as they've given up 4.9 yards per carry to opposing running backs this season.

Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals face the Commanders in an interconference clash on Monday Night Football in Week 11. He corralled 11 of 14 targets for a season-high 231 yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory. After failing to eclipse the 100-yard mark through his first six outings, Chase has done so in three consecutive contests, gaining more than 140 receiving yards in each. He'll take a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets into a matchup against Washington's 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (33.5) to WRs.

Keenan Allen is coming off an impactful 49ers debut heading into a Week 11 matchup versus Minnesota. After being acquired by San Francisco at the trade deadline, Allen caught five of seven targets for 61 yards this past Sunday in a win over Dallas. Despite having a relatively short amount of time to learn his new team's offense, Allen looked to have good chemistry with QB Brock Purdy, which is an encouraging sign for his production moving forward. His work as a possession receiver could be especially useful against the Vikings, who own the highest blitz rate in the NFL.

Roschon Johnson is likely to be a depth option as the Bears play New Orleans in Week 11. Johnson has mostly benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb), but he didn't play a snap on offense in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay, even with Monangai remaining inactive. Monangai could also return in the upcoming home front, which would shrink Johnson's role even more. The Saints have ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs, but Johnson's fluctuating role makes him a tough play.

Tank Dell had just 21 yards on four targets in the Week 10 loss to Cleveland after turning nine targets into 105 yards and a TD in Houston's Week 9 win over the Chargers. The speedy wideout continues to offer big-play potential in Week 11 against the Colts, who give up 15.4 yards per catch to wide receivers. Dell's floor is low in Houston's deep WR room, but his ceiling is certainly high enough to warrant flex consideration, especially with surging QB C.J. Stroud having thrown 13 touchdown passes in the Texans' last four games.

Jeremiyah Love has missed Arizona's past two games due to an ankle injury but could return in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love is slated to practice this week, though that doesn't guarantee that he'll suit up versus Dallas. If the rookie running back misses another game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would likely continue to split the Cardinals' backfield work. Arizona's ground game could be set for a big day against a Dallas defense that is giving up 20.9 fantasy points per game to running backs, seventh-worst in the league.

news.text: Arizona placed Love (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.. Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.

He will have his work cut out for him in Week 11 versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 91 rushing yards per clash, which is sixth in the NFL. In addition, the Jags have surrendered only five rushing touchdowns this season, which is tied for fourth in the league.

Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

Rhamondre Stevenson is uncertain to suit up for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury. New England fell into a big hole in Week 9, limiting Stevenson's carries prior to the injury, and he finished with a season-low six for the third time this season. His passing game involvement included a second touchdown reception in three weeks. If he plays, Stevenson figures to again lead the Patriots' backfield since TreVeyon Henderson will also likely be sidelined. Stevenson's rushing yard expectations can be tempered against a defense that's allowing a mere 3.9 yards per carry.

Malik Nabers had a costly fumble last game for the Giants. Nabers had the ball punched out of his hands in scoring territory versus the Commanders, who ultimately defeated the G-Men by a score of 24-21. Nabers has now been held under 50 yards receiving in each of the last two outings following a dazzling four-game stretch of 100-yard outbursts. In Week 11, he will look to rebound against a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.

Amon-Ra St. Brown will seek to stay hot as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. St. Brown finally broke his touchdown drought in a Week 10 blowout win over New England, catching four of five targets for 98 yards and two scores. The star pass catcher has now posted a 65-755-7 receiving line on 91 targets across nine contests. He'll face a Tampa Bay defense that's ranked 11th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season.

However, he ranked first on the team in targets while the rest of Carolina's receiver room combined for five targets, which is positive sign for McMillan's fantasy outlook going forward. Bo Nix comes out of the Broncos' bye having built up a bit of momentum, producing multiple touchdowns in three straight games prior to the break while turning the ball over only once during that stretch. The third-year quarterback didn't get any reinforcements at the trade deadline, but the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman in the backfield gives Denver a legitimate running option to help balance the offense, and second-year wideout Pat Bryant returned from IR right before the bye. In Week 11, Nix will take aim at a Raiders defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

Christian McCaffrey enters San Francisco's Week 11 matchup against Minnesota on the heels of one of the biggest performances of his career. In this past Sunday's win over Dallas, McCaffrey recorded a career-best 161 receiving yards en route to 223 total yards and three touchdowns. The star RB has logged at least one TD in each of his past eight games and has multiple scores in three of his past four contests, making him an elite week-to-week fantasy asset. Metcalf found the end zone for just the second time all season and the first time since Week 3. Brown finally found paydirt, doing so for the first time since Week 1, while recording his first two receiving scores of the season. He'll look to exploit a Commanders defense that gave up 78 yards and two TDs to Cam Skattebo in their previous outing.

Hunter Henry figures to be a popular option for the Patriots in Week 10 against a Lions defense that struggles against opposing tight ends. Henry has just three targets in each of his last two games and has topped 48 yards just twice all season, but Week 10 presents an inviting opportunity. Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to tight ends and 8.2 yards per target, the highest numbers across the league. With New England potentially missing its top two running backs, a pass-heavy script would set Henry up for top-end production.

Chig Okonkwo has been a frequent target of quarterback Jayden Daniels since returning from injury for the Commanders. Okonkwo has at least six targets in four of the last five contests for Washington.  In fact, Okonkwo has been targeted 15 times over the last two games alone. Okonkwo is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, though. In Week 11, he will face a fairly stingy Cincinnati pass defense. The Bengals are allowing only 216.2 passing yards per clash, which is 11th in the league. Likewise, Cincy has given up just 11 throwing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

Caleb Williams will look to stay solid as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Williams pieced together another solid outing in Chicago's Week 8 MNF win over the Seahawks, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown. The starting quarterback has now thrown for 860 yards and four touchdowns in his last three games, and he's passed for 240 or more yards in all but one outing this season. He'll shift focus to a Tampa Bay squad that's ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

Josh Allen faces potential workload limitations in the Bills' Week 11 game against the Dolphins. Allen completed only 11 of 21 passes against the Jets in Week 10, his second-lowest volume of the season, as Buffalo was able to get out to a comfortable lead and not challenge the Jets through the air. Another potentially uncompetitive game seems to be looming, and while Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns to go with his 13 passing scores, Miami has allowed quarterbacks to run for just two touchdowns all season. Allen routinely gets his fantasy points, but Week 11 expectations can be tempered slightly

Matt Gay didn't get much volume in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, as he converted both his field goal attempts and his only PAT. The veteran kicker has handled two or fewer FG attempts in four of the last six games, but with rookie Fernando Mendoza replacing Kirk Cousins under center, the offense's efficiency could take a step backward and give Gay more field goal chances. He may not be much busier in Week 11 against a Broncos team allowing 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league.

news.text: Gay (hip) didn't practice Thursday.. Gay was limited Wednesday, so the kicker's downgrade in participation a day later clouds his status for Sunday's game against the Broncos. With that in mind, the Raiders had Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo in for tryouts Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

players.outlook: Harrison Mevis' job may be on the line heading into the Rams' Week 6 contest against the Cardinals. Mevis missed both of his field-goal attempts in Week 5 on Monday Night Football, including a 50-yarder in the first quarter and a blocked 48-yarder in overtime that could have won the game. He's now just 5-for-9 on FG tries this season, including 3-for-6 from 40-to-49 yards out. Should Mevis still be kicking for the Rams in Week 6, he may be limited mostly to extra points versus a Cardinals defense that has yielded 18 PAT tries to just six FG attempts this season.

Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns welcome the Texans to town for a Week 10 AFC clash. He caught both of his targets for 42 yards, including an impressive 39-yard touchdown in overtime, during Cleveland's 23-22 OT loss in Week 9. Fannin was quiet until the extra frame, a disappointing development after he erupted for a 10-154-0 line on 12 targets in his previous outing. He'll look to stay hot despite a difficult matchup versus Houston's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (10.1) to TEs.

C.J. Stroud tossed three more touchdown passes in Houston's Week 10 loss to the Browns, bringing his TD:INT ratio to 19:3 through nine games, with 13 of those scores coming in his last four outings. The fourth-year QB's brilliance has largely been wasted on the 3-6 Texans, as the defense and running game have both declined from last season. Houston's playoff hopes aren't extinguished yet, but Stroud can't afford a Week 11 letdown in a home rematch against a Colts defense that held him to 167 yards and one TD in Week 3, when the Texans lost 19-17 at Indianapolis. The 3-7 Colts have allowed a 16

J.K. Dobbins fell into a depth role behind rookie Jonah Coleman in the Broncos' backfield prior to the team's bye. Over the last three games, Dobbins has 17 carries to Coleman's 37, and the youngster is also seeing the bulk of the action at the goal line. Dobbins scored a rushing TD during that span, and he hasn't completely disappeared from the game plan, but it would likely take an injury to Coleman for him to log significant volume again. Dobbins will take on a Raiders defense in Week 11 that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Rome Odunze will aim to build on a season-best showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Odunze notched his first touchdown of the season and paired it with four catches for 60 yards in a Week 9 win over Tampa Bay before Chicago's bye week. The third-year pass catcher has now logged 32 receptions for 528 yards and a touchdown across nine games this season. He'll take on a New Orleans squad that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

Jakobi Meyers ranks second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington in both receiving yards (408) and targets (43), but the gap between Washington and Meyers is far larger than the gap between Meyers and TE Brenton Strange for the role of Trevor Lawrence's No. 2 target. Meyers has exceeded 65 yards just once all season and hasn't scored since Week 3, so he has been a disappointment more often than not for fantasy managers plugging him into a flex spot. He'll have a decent opportunity to end his six-game touchdown drought in Week 11 against a Giants secondary that has allowed WRs to score 11 tim

news.text: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.. Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

players.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers travel to take on the Eagles in Week 11. He had seven carries for 15 yards and caught five of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Warren and the entire Steelers offense found little success until the game was already out of reach, as several backups took the field in the fourth quarter. Warren will look to shake off the tough outing, but he'll have to do so against Philadelphia's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to opposing RBs.

James Cook brings an eight-game scoring streak into the Bills' Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He has at least 18 carries in five straight games and has topped 100 rushing yards in five of nine outings overall. Cook hasn't caught a pass in two weeks, an area where Miami has been vulnerable, allowing five touchdown receptions to running backs, the same number of rushing touchdowns they've surrendered. A quick turnaround to a Week 12 Thursday night game is the only concern for Cook's workload and high-end production.

Justin Jefferson could be in store for better output again as the Vikings play San Francisco in Week 11. Jefferson benefited from the addition of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota in a Week 10 win over Green Bay, logging season highs in catches (9) and targets (13). The star wideout's 74 yards were also his best total since Week 5, further supporting that he may be in store for a return to dominance. He'll take on a 49ers defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this campaign.

Garrett Wilson continues to dominate targets in the Jets' passing game ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. He garnered a season-high 14 targets in Week 10, his fourth outing with double-digit looks, while topping 100 yards for the third time. Wilson has only three touchdowns on the year and faces a bit of quarterback uncertainty with Geno Smith dealing with an ankle injury, but the Chargers have allowed 11 receivers to score in nine games and have surrendered 340-plus passing yards in consecutive weeks. With steady volume, Wilson profiles as a safe lineup cog in Week 11.

Jordyn Tyson will look to build on his breakout performance in the Saints' Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Tyson was one of New Orleans' few bright spots in the Week 11 loss to the Panthers, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in his second NFL game. He's clearly established himself as one of the Saints' top two receiving options but could struggle if Chris Olave is more involved in Week 11. Tyson could thrive against a solid Bears secondary, however, as they have allowed 9.2 yards per target to opposing WRs this year.

news.text: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.. Tyson maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a chest injury in the wake of his 11-80-0 line on 13 targets from the second game of his career this past Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

players.outlook: Chad Ryland and a sputtering Arizona offense will face off against Kansas City in Week 11. Ryland accounted for all of Arizona's scoring this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams with a pair of field goals. The Cardinals managed just 123 total yards in the contest, which was rookie quarterback Carson Beck's NFL debut. Arizona doesn't figure to pour on the points against a KC defense that is allowing the third-fewest points (17.3) in the league, so Ryland could see limited opportunities again Sunday.

Kyren Williams may be asked to log a heftier workload than usual for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Williams rushed for just 45 yards -- his second-lowest mark of the season -- on 15 carries against Washington in Week 9, adding 16 yards on three catches. However, Los Angeles is going to be without wideout Puka Nacua (knee) for multiple weeks, and with Davante Adams (hamstring) still on IR, the team may turn more to its ground game  -- led by Williams and Blake Corum -- to carry the load. Arizona's defense has been middling against the run this season, allowing 18.0 fantasy points p

news.text: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.. Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown

players.outlook: Ladd McConkey missed his third game of the season in Week 10, this time due to back trouble, as the Chargers' beat the Ravens for their first win of the season. McConkey's been fully healthy for only two games so far in 2026, posting an 8-152-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, and his only touchdown of the year came back in the first half of Week 1 before he suffered his initial rib injury, which was followed by a foot injury and a concussion. If McConkey is cleared to return in Week 11, he'll face a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

news.text: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.. McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

players.outlook: Colston Loveland will remain a top option in Chicago's passing game against the Saints in Week 11. Loveland has seen success lately after a shaky start to the season, surpassing 50 yards in his last four games and finding the end zone twice in that stretch. The second-year tight end has now posted a 37-363-2 receiving line off 57 targets in the first nine outings of the season. He'll face a New Orleans defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

news.text: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.. Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

players.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson has scored in three consecutive games heading into Houston's Week 11 home game against the Colts. He's averaging six targets per game, and while his paltry average of 6.4 yards per target suggests C.J. Stroud would be better off distributing those looks elsewhere, Hutchinson's volume has propelled the 26-year-old wideout into the weekly flex conversation. Perhaps Hutchinson is just a late bloomer who is finding his groove, but it's fair to remain skeptical considering his three TDs in the last three games match his total of three TDs from 55 regular-season appearances before

Isaiah Likely notched a career-high 127 yards receiving last game for the Giants. Likely reeled in nine passes, one of which went for a 66-yard touchdown, though the G-Men fell to Washington by a score of 24-21. Still, Likely has scored in back-to-back contests, and has five scores in his last five outings.  In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL. However, Jacksonville has surrendered just 10 passing scores this season, which is fourth in the NFL.

D'Andre Swift will look to bounce back from a tough showing as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Swift was shelled by a tough Tampa Bay front before Chicago's Week 10 bye, rushing the ball 12 times for 31 yards. The veteran still racked up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games without Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) out, so there is still hope for him to deliver moving forward. Even if Monangai returns, New Orleans ranking 31st in fantasy points allowed to running backs could allow for an entire backfield to eat.

Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

news.text: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.. With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

players.outlook: DeMario Douglas will look to continue his recent surge when the Patriots face the Lions in Week 10. Douglas had a season-high 102 yards on nine targets in Week 9, a game that developed into a pass-heavy shootout. A similar game script could be on tap against a Detroit defense that has allowed the fourth-most passing yards. A potential return for A.J. Brown may reduce Douglas' targets, but with the expectation the Patriots will throw often, he can post 65 yards or better for the sixth time in seven weeks.

news.text: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.. The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a ham

players.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 10 matchup against the Chiefs. Robinson was one of Atlanta's few bright spots during the Week 9 loss to the Bengals, accumulating 147 yards and a touchdown on 25 touches. The Texas product is currently averaging the third-most touches per game (22.2) in the NFL, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top running backs despite a tough matchup. Kansas City's defense has given up just 20.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through eight games this year.

news.text: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.. The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

players.outlook: Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

Tony Pollard has racked up 391 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns over Tennessee's last three games, putting him in the fantasy RB1 conversation for a Week 11 trip to Dallas. After a pair of dominant rushing performances, Pollard struggled to find running room against Jacksonville's elite front in Week 10 but racked up 66 receiving yards and a TD on a career-high eight catches. The former Cowboys RB is locked into a workhorse role for the Titans, and Pollard's old team has given up the most fantasy production in the league to RBs, allowing 155 scrimmage yards per game, as well as a league-high

players.outlook: Jonathan Taylor exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in 10 tries during the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins, but he was held without a touchdown for a third consecutive game. Seth McGowan has two rushing TDs during Taylor's three-game drought, both of which came from inside the 5-yard line. The rookie seventh-round pick could remain a thorn in Taylor's side if the Colts continue to give McGowan goal-line opportunities.
