Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

news.text: Hill's (knee) agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver hasn't yet been medically cleared but is expected to be "in a few weeks," James Palmer of Bleacher Report reports.. Though his outlook hasn't changed much since Rosenhaus last provided an update in mid-October, Hill is seemingly getting closer to being ready to take the field. It's unclear what type of interest Hill has garnered around the league, but he's a free agent and could hold some appeal for teams once doctors give him the green light to play.

players.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to battle the Eagles for an interconference clash in Week 11. He corralled one of three targets for five yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss, playing a season-low 50% of the offensive snaps. That can largely be attributed to the game being well out of hand for the Steelers, who trailed 31-3 going into the fourth quarter. Washington will aim to make more of an impact versus Philadelphia's stingy defense against TEs, as they're tied for the fourth-fewest fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to the position.

Devaughn Vele is expected to operate as the Saints' No. 3 wideout during the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Since 2026 first-round pick Jordyn Tyson returned from injury in the Week 9 win over the Browns, Vele has caught just four of six targets for 31 yards. It appears as if his role on New Orleans' offense has diminished, suggesting his fantasy value is limited without scoring a touchdown on a weekly basis. He's set to face a solid Chicago secondary in Week 11 that's given up just eight receiving touchdowns to wideouts through nine games this season.

Malachi Fields has caught at least two passes in every game during his rookie campaign for the Giants. In fact, he caught three passes for 62 yards last game, and has at least four targets in four-straight tilts. In Week 11, the Giants will face a Jacksonville defense that has been mediocre against the pass in 2026. The Jags are allowing 228.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 19th in the NFL.

Pat Bryant returned from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury in the Broncos' final game before their Week 10 bye, catching four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. It was his most productive outing of the season, but it also came as Jaylen Waddle left the contest early with a concussion. Bryant has shown some chemistry with Bo Nix, but assuming Waddle doesn't miss additional time, his target volume figures to remain limited. Bryant will try to return to the end zone in Week 11 against a Raiders secondary that ranks 24th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Mack Hollins' opportunities for the Patriots in Week 10 against the Lions appear unsettled with A.J. Brown (knee) potentially returning to action. Hollins returned from a four-week absence in Week 9, catching half of his six targets and finding the end zone for the first time all season. While Detroit's secondary has been picked on often and allows 8.0 yards per target, Hollins doesn't have a clear path to heavy volume, leading to big-play or touchdown dependency.

Tutu Atwell will have a chance to step into a larger role for the Rams in Week 10 against Arizona. Atwell has logged a modest four catches for 68 yards on nine targets over his past two games after going catchless in Week 7. However, Puka Nacua is expected to land on IR due to a knee injury, so the Rams are going to need to look to other wideouts, potentially including Atwell, to step up in the passing game. A matchup against the Cardinals presents a good opportunity, as they rank 24th in the NFL with 22.2 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.

Kayshon Boutte crashed back down to earth with a zero-catch performance in Week 10 against the Browns. That season-worst outing followed a 125-yard, two-TD outburst in Week 9 against the Chargers. Boutte's likely to land somewhere in between those two extremes in Week 11 against the Colts, though the Week 10 goose egg is closer to what should be expected of the depth wideout. He's averaging just 24 receiving yards in the eight games excluding his effort against the Chargers, with no TDs as a member of the Texans outside of that outing, either.

news.text: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.. The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

players.outlook: Michael Mayer could be set for a significant role in the Raiders' passing game in the short term. In a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks, Brock Bowers suffered an ankle injury, and while it's not thought to be serious, he could be sidelined for a game or two. Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards against Seattle, but his volume from rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza would likely increase with Bowers off the field. If Mayer's volume does increase in Week 11, it will come against a Broncos defense that ranks 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Dalton Schultz is coming off a bittersweet Week 10 performance against the Browns. He scored his first touchdown of the season on his only catch but was held to a single reception for the first time all season. The reliable TE is a borderline fantasy starter for Week 11 against the Colts; however, there are certainly higher-upside options to be found at the position. Schultz hasn't topped 45 yards since his 140-yard Week 2 outburst, which occurred while the Texans were without top WR Nico Collins, who has since recovered from a hamstring injury. Quentin Johnston was nearly invisible in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, catching his only target for six yards. Ladd McConkey missed the contest with a back issue, and in his absence, Tre' Harris stepped up as Justin Herbert's top downfield option. Johnston has just a single reception in four of his last five games, and his skill set seems to be a particularly poor fit for Mike McDaniel's quick-strike passing attack. He's unlikely to contribute much in Week 11 against a Jets secondary that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Washington for a Week 11 tilt on Monday Night Football. He caught one of two targets for nine yards during Cincinnati's Week 10 victory, unable to capitalize on Joe Burrow throwing for 409 yards and four TDs. Gesicki now sports a 3-20-0 receiving line on four targets over his last two outings after catching a touchdown in each of his five previous games. He does, however, get a favorable matchup versus a Commanders defense allowing 20.2 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing TEs.

Darius Cooper had a season-high eight targets last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he managed just two catches for 25 yards despite the extra looks. DeVonta Smith and/or Dontayvion Wicks could return from  injury following the bye, which would shift Cooper back down the depth chart despite the favorable Week 11 matchup with the Steelers. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

Calvin Ridley (hip) sat out for the Titans in Week 7 against the Browns. Even if he returns for Week 8 against the Bengals, Ridley won't be a viable fantasy option. He has caught a pass in only three of six appearances this season, with season totals of five catches for 81 yards while operating in a depth role at WR.

Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of the Saints' top pass catchers in the Week 11 matchup against the Bears. Johnson has really struggled over New Orleans' last four games, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. With Jordyn Tyson breaking out in the Week 10 loss to the Panthers (11-80-0), Johnson will likely receive even less opportunities going forward. He likely needs to score a touchdown to find fantasy relevance in Week 11 against a Bears defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to tight ends all season.

AJ Barner will look to build upon his two-touchdown game when Seattle visits Las Vegas in Week 10. Barner had one score through the air and another on the ground in a Week 9 win over Arizona.  Though his receiving output has remained modest, Barner has been getting more opportunities to carry the ball in short-yardage situations in recent weeks, as he's logged six carries over his past three games. He'll seek to get into the end zone against the Raiders, who have given up the second-most TDs (eight) to tight ends this season.

Travis Hunter generated 59 of his 91 receiving yards and his only touchdown of the campaign in Week 6 against the Texans. The 2025 second overall pick has the talent to produce a big play or two in any given game despite his limited usage on offense, but he has focused primarily on playing cornerback throughout his second NFL season. With Jacksonville's receiving corps healthy for Week 11 against the Giants, expect Hunter to remain off the fantasy radar, playing just a handful of snaps on offense.

Rashod Bateman and the Ravens visit the Panthers for a Week 11 interconference tilt. He caught three of five targets for 42 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. The receptions, yardage and targets were the most for Bateman since he recorded a 5-62-0 line on six targets in Week 5. Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards in his team debut, so there's at least some shred of possibility the Ravens can evolve into a more pass-friendly offense, but fantasy managers need Bateman to put up much bigger numbers before they consider starting him.

Dontayvion Wicks could return from an ankle issue for the Eagles following their bye. Wicks has missed three-straight games for Philadelphia due to the ailment. His return, along with that of DeVonta Smith, would bolster an extremely depleted wide receiving corps. If he can suit up, the matchup could also be favorable in Week 11, as the Steelers defense has been surprisingly vulnerable to the pass in 2026. Pittsburgh is allowing 242.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.

news.text: Wicks (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.. As was fellow WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who worked fully Thursday. Wicks -- who last played in Week 6 -- has logged consecutive 'LPs' thus far this week, but if he upgrades to full participation Friday he'd be positioned to head into Sunday's game against the Steelers without an injury designation.

players.outlook: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

news.text: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.. While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly afte

players.outlook: De'Zhaun Stribling isn't likely to play in San Francisco's Week 2 matchup versus Miami. Stribling suffered an ankle injury during his NFL debut last Thursday against the Rams and is expected to miss at least a month of action. While he's out, Demarcus Robinson is slated to take on the 49ers' No. 3 wideout role.

news.text: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.. This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

players.outlook: Tyler Higbee may need to ramp up his production for the Rams' passing game to be successful, beginning with a Week 10 matchup in Arizona. Higbee continued his recent trend of limited production this past Sunday against Washington, logging just one catch for 13 yards on five targets. He's recorded two or fewer receptions in three straight games, but Los Angeles may need Higbee to be more impactful after losing star WR Puka Nacua for what is likely to be multiple weeks due to a knee injury. The Cardinals rank 27th in the NFL with 10.4 fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends this season.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching d

news.text: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.. After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. players.outlook: Terry McLaurin returned to the lineup for Washington following a one-game absence due to a hamstring issue. McLaurin led the squad in receiving with 62 yards on four catches in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Fellow wideout Stefon Diggs was inactive with a hamstring ailment of his own, and if Diggs misses more time, McLaurin would certainly benefit in terms of additional looks. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns

news.text: McLaurin (knee) underwent surgery Friday to repair the torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.. The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.

players.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the 3-5 Texans in Week 10. He caught two of four targets for 37 yards during Week 9's overtime loss to the Saints. Through nine contests this season, Jeudy has amassed a modest 18-208-0 line on 28 targets. He remains off the fantasy radar despite a favorable matchup versus a Houston defense allowing 38.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs, which ranks 30th.

Treylon Burks returned from a foot injury following a one-game absence for Washington. He managed two catches for 27 yards in the 24-21 win over the Giants. Burks had three targets for the game. However, in Week 11, he will be facing a Bengals defense allowing just 216.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. In addition, Cincy has yielded only 11 passing scores, which is tied for fifth in the NFL.

Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

news.text: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.. Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation would at least keep him off season-ending injured reserve, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Ada

players.outlook: Rashid Shaheed (knee) has missed Seattle's past two games and isn't certain to return in Week 10 against the Raiders. Shaheed hasn't practiced since getting hurt in Week 7, and he'll likely need to return to at least a few limited sessions before being ready to play in games again. Should Shaheed sit out another contest, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton will likely continue to be the Seahawks' top wideouts behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If Shaheed can suit up, though, he'll face a Raiders defense that has allowed 27 passing plays of 20-plus yards this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

Keon Coleman isn't factoring heavily in the Bills' passing game entering a Week 11 matchup with the Dolphins. He was held to just one catch on three targets in Week 10, the fifth time in nine games he's secured just one reception, creating a low floor for the team's third receiving option. While Miami allows a generous 9.3 yards per target, they've surrendered only six touchdowns to wide receivers. Buffalo remains a run-heavy offense and likely won't need to throw often in Week 11 to beat an overmatched opponent, further limiting Coleman's chances.

Cooper Kupp continues to be quiet this season ahead of Seattle's Week 10 visit to Las Vegas. Kupp logged a 3-32-0 receiving line this past Sunday against Arizona despite Rashid Shaheed (knee) continuing to be sidelined. Kupp's four targets in the game were actually his third-most through nine games, emphasizing how little attention he's gotten from the Seahawks' quarterbacks this season. With that said, he at least has a good matchup coming up, as the Raiders have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season -- tied for second-most in the NFL.

Brian Thomas tied his season high with three catches in Week 10 against the Titans, but he produced just 29 yards and remains an afterthought in Jacksonville's prolific passing game. The 2024 first-round pick has just 13 receptions in nine games during what has been a disappointing third NFL season. With Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers both healthy and clearly ahead of him on the WR depth chart, Thomas has minimal fantasy appeal for a Week 11 matchup against a stingy Giants secondary. Even if one of Washington or Meyers were to get hurt, it's unclear if Thomas would inherit additional oppo

Roman Wilson and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He failed to catch his only target prior to exiting Pittsburgh's 34-22 win in Week 5 with a finger injury. Wilson has already been ruled out for the trip to Tampa Bay, meaning Germie Bernard should see a boost in playing time and opportunities in his absence.

news.text: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.. With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over th

players.outlook: Konata Mumpfield may need to step up for the Rams in Week 10 against the Cardinals. Mumpfield has been quiet of late, logging no more than two catches and 20 yards over his past six games. However, with Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua (knee) expected to join him there, Los Angeles is likely going to need some of its other wideouts to start being more productive. Mumpfield has a good matchup against Arizona, as the Cardinals have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts, tied for second-most in the NFL.

Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Vikings in Week 10. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

news.text: The Packers officially placed Reed (neck) on injured reserve Wednesday.. Coach Matt LaFleur announced earlier Wednesday that Reed required surgery on his neck injury that'll be season-ending, so this transaction was inevitable. Reed has been contained to just nine regular-season appearances the last two years due to health concerns, but LaFleur did relay to Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that he doesn't believe the current issue will threaten the wide receiver's career. With Reed sidelined for the rest of the campaign, Skyy Moore will operate as Green Bay's No. 3 WR behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

players.outlook: Malik Washington's opportunities continue to decline as the Dolphins get set to face the Bills in Week 11. Washington recorded three targets in Week 10, the third time in four weeks since Miami's Week 6 bye that he's failed to garner more looks. While Miami figures to throw from behind against Buffalo, Kyle McCord spread his 32 pass attempts in Week 10 across 11 different options, all while rookie Chris Bell was sidelined. With just one touchdown catch all season, Washington doesn't seem likely to pop against a defense that's allowed 11 touchdown catches to wide receivers, the fourth-highest t

In Week 11, Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are on the road for an interconference clash with the Panthers. He hauled in three of 11 targets for 61 yards during Baltimore's Week 10 loss. The rookie third-rounder set new career highs in yardage and targets, finishing third on the team in yardage and first in targets. Jacoby Brissett attempted 49 passes and threw for 340 yards in his team debut, and if the Ravens continue to throw at that rate, Lane could certainly develop into an intriguing fantasy prospect. However, managers need the rookie to convert his looks into real production, and his usage

Elic Ayomanor led the Titans with 79 receiving yards on 10 targets in the Week 10 loss against the Jaguars, as Carnell Tate (shoulder) didn't play and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exited early. If one or both of Tate and Robinson remain unavailable in Week 11, Ayomanor could make the most of another expanded role against a Dallas defense that's giving up 158 yards per game to WRs and has allowed 10 receiving TDs to the position in as many games. If you're considering Ayomanor for a flex spot in Week 11, keep in mind that he averaged just 25 receiving yards per game when Tate and Robinson were bot

Kalif Raymond will remain a secondary option in the passing game in Week 11 as the Bears play the Saints. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has petered out with just one game over 20 receiving yards since Week 3. The veteran will take a 32-290-1 receiving line into a tough matchup against a New Orleans defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

Gavin Bartholomew will look to build on a career-best game as the Vikings play the 49ers in Week 11. Bartholomew benefited from veteran T.J. Hockenson being out with a wrist injury in Week 10, bringing in three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. The rookie has now posted a 10-90-1 receiving line across nine games. The 49ers have ranked 19th in fantasy points allowed to TEs this campaign.

Jake Bates will look to stay reliable as the Lions play the Buccaneers in Week 11. Bates didn't attempt a field goal in a Week 10 win over the Patriots, but 5 XPAs kept his performance solid. The starting boot has now converted 16 of 17 field-goal attempts and made all 29 of his extra-point tries across nine games this campaign. He'll face a Tampa defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers.

Oronde Gadsden had a tough night in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens. He missed a good chunk of the first half after getting poked in the eye and ultimately played just 11 snaps on offense, catching his only target for seven yards. The second-year tight end is still a dangerous receiver, but his subpar blocking skills limit his role in Mike McDaniel's offense, and the return of David Njoku from IR creates further competition for snaps and targets. Gadsden could struggle to make a splash in Week 11, even against a Jets defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Eli Raridon is trending favorably ahead of the Patriots' Week 10 matchup against a Lions defense that struggles against tight ends. Raridon has collected at least four targets in three straight games, even with fellow tight end Hunter Henry healthy, and the Lions are allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. While still a secondary option in New England's passing game, Raridon can garner enough attention to be a viable option in a plus matchup.

Ka'imi Fairbairn is 19-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-24 on PAT tries for the Texans heading into a Week 11 home game against the Colts. Indianapolis is tied for the second-most made field goals allowed (21) and is surrendering 27.1 points per game overall. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter at the kicker position, as usual, in Week 11 as the 3-6 Texans try to bolster their dwindling playoff hopes.

Cairo Santos will look to build on a solid showing as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Santos made all of his kicks in Chicago's Week 8 win over the Seahawks, nailing two field goal attempts and four XPAs. The veteran kicker had also missed a field goal in three straight games before this matchup, so he's hopefully now back on track. Tampa Bay has ranked 13th in fantasy points allowed to kickers so far this campaign.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

Noah Gray logged three targets in Kansas City's Week 10 win over the Falcons, the fifth time in the last seven games the 27-year-old tight end has gotten that much volume. While his role is limited behind Travis Kelce, Gray managed a 15-185-1 line on 18 targets over that seven-game stretch, and he's been able to build a decent floor despite a lack of ceiling. He'll look for his second touchdown of the season in Week 11 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

Zach Ertz caught two passes last game for the Eagles, as he continues to fill in for his injured former understudy, Dallas Goedert. It appears that Goedert is unlikely to suit up in  Week 5 versus the Jags. Philadelphia's passing offense struggled mightily without Goedert and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith, and the early departure of Saquon Barkley due to an injury of his own did not help matters. Ertz had four targets last game and could prove a useful safety valve with an otherwise young, inexperienced pass-catching corps. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags. In Week 11, Chris Boswell and the Steelers are back on the road to face the 2-7 Eagles. He connected on his only field goal attempt and lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss in Week 10. The Steelers offense struggled mightily to gain any traction until the game was well out of reach, leaving Boswell on the sidelines while his team opted to go for two on their final touchdown. He'll look to get more involved against a Philadelphia defense giving up 24.6 points per game this season.

Jason Sanders surged into fantasy relevance for an inefficient Jets offense ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Chargers. The Jets have been kept out of the end zone in consecutive games, forcing Sanders to kick four field goals in each outing, something he's now done in four of their last five games. Sanders has double-digit scoring potential against a defense that's allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game to opposing kickers.

Cameron Dicker booted three field goals for a third straight game, and the fifth time in the last seven, as the Chargers recorded their first win of 2026 in a Week 10 victory over the Ravens. The team's offensive struggles have created extra FG opportunities for its kicker, and Dicker has yet to kick more than two PATs in a game even as his field goal volume remains steady. That gives him a somewhat reliable floor, but a questionable ceiling, heading into a Week 11 clash with a Jets team allowing 25.4 points a contest, 22nd in the league.

So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

David Njoku returned from a six-game absence due to a fractured fibula in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens, playing 17 snaps on offense but failing to get a target. The veteran tight end had a productive Week 1 before getting hurt in Week 2, and his combination of pass-catching and blocking skills makes him a better fit for Mike McDaniel's scheme than Oronde Gadsden. Charlie Kolar will remain atop the depth chart for now, but Njoku could push for that spot as he shakes off his rust. He'll look to take on a bigger role in Week 11 against a Jets defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

Cole Kmet will stay out as the Bears play the Saints in Week 11. Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury at the end of Chicago's Week 7 win over the Patriots. He's now been placed on IR and will officially sit out for the rest of the year. Kmet's absence should continue to increase rookie tight end Sam Roush's usage.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

Greg Dulcich faces an uphill battle for meaningful production in the Dolphins' Week 11 game against the Bills. He had two straight appealing matchups with the Lions and Colts in Weeks 9 and 10, and turned that into just two catches for 14 yards. With suspect quarterback play and a matchup with a Buffalo defense that's allowed just one tight end to score against them in nine games, Dulcich can only be useful for lineups in deeper formats.

The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

In Week 11, Evan McPherson and the high-flying Bengals offense will travel to Washington for an interconference showdown. He went 1-for-2 on field goals while connecting on all five PATs during Cincinnati's 38-18 win in Week 10. McPherson's miss was his first of the season, so he'll be looking to get back on track versus a Commanders team allowing 24.8 points per game.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

Dominic Zvada somehow still has a job following yet another missed field goal for the Giants. Zvada missed a 33-yarder in the 24-21 loss to the Commanders. He has missed six field goals to date, including three from under 50 yards out. In Week 11, points will likely be difficult to come by versus the Jags. Jacksonville is allowing just 16 points per tilt, which is second in the NFL.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

Tommy Tremble is expected to remain one of Carolina's top tight ends during the Week 11 matchup against the Ravens. Tremble logged his second consecutive four reception game during the Week 10 win over the Saints, accumulating 48 receiving yards on five targets. On the season, he's caught 25 of 34 targets for 227 yards and three touchdowns (tied for the second-most on the Panthers). Despite being relatively productive, Tremble remains the Panthers' No. 2 tight end as a pass catcher, with Darren Waller receiving the majority of the work. Tremble could still find success in Week 11, as the Raven

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

Colby Parkinson could be a big part of the Rams' passing game in Week 10 against Arizona. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles with four catches against Washington this past Sunday, though he gained just 13 yards on those receptions. Still, the Rams are going to need some pass catchers to step up in the wake of a knee injury that is likely going to cause star wideout Puka Nacua to miss multiple games, and Parkinson has tallied at least four catches in each of the last three games in which he's played. The Cardinals have struggled against tight ends, giving up six receiving touchdowns, tied f

Evan Engram tied his season highs with four catches on five targets in Week 9, the Broncos' last game before their bye. The veteran tight end has caught one pass or fewer in five of nine games this year, and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1. With Denver's WR corps potentially fully healthy for the first time all season, Engram's role as a pass catcher could be even more limited. He'll try to make a difference in Week 11 against a Raiders defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top receiving options during the Week 11 matchup against the Lions. Otton received a season-high eight targets in the Week 9 loss to the Bears, logging four receptions for 25 yards. On the season, he ranks third on the Buccaneers in targets (38) and receptions (23) while ranking fourth in receiving yards (211). Otton could really thrive in Week 11, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 22.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the most in the NFL.

Gunnar Helm has exceeded 28 receiving yards just once in the Titans' first nine games this season and has yet to score a TD. However, he has 12 catches in the last three games after recording just nine receptions through six games. The second-year TE is trending in the right direction ahead of a Week 11 matchup with a Dallas defense that ranks in the middle of the pack at defending the position, largely because opponents haven't had to involve their TEs as much while carving up the Cowboys' defense with RB and WR production. Mason Taylor brings low volume in an otherwise promising matchup in Week 11 when the Jets face the Chargers. Taylor hasn't collected more than six targets all season while topping 33 yards just once, but with Omar Cooper (ankle) potentially sidelined, more targets could be available in Week 11. The Chargers have allowed only one touchdown to tight ends but have surrendered over 100 yards to the position twice in the last four weeks, giving Mason potential for a yardage uptick.

Chase McLaughlin could have limited scoring opportunities in the Buccaneers' Week 11 matchup against the Lions. McLaughlin has been one of fantasy's top kickers through nine games this season, converting on all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 18 of his point-after attempts. Despite this, he could have few scoring chances in Week 11 against a Detroit defense that's given up just 5.3 kicking points per game on the season.

Harrison Butker hasn't converted a field goal attempt in two straight games and hasn't kicked more than one in four straight, going a weak 2-for-6 on attempts during that stretch. The Kansas City offense has been providing him with more PATs, however, and he's gone 13-for-13 on extra points over the last three contests. Butker's struggles have left him with little job security, but for now he still holds the job. He could be busier in Week 11 against a Cardinals team allowing 28.9 points per game, tied for 31st in the league with the Raiders.

Brevyn Spann-Ford caught a 26-yard pass for Dallas last game. Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker are splitting reps at tight end due to the injury to Jake Ferguson. While Spann-Ford was targeted three times, Schoonmaker was targeted twice. By contrast, the top three wideouts for the Cowboys combined for a staggering 38 targets in the 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Spann-Ford remains a high-risk option in Week 11 versus the Titans despite the favorable matchup. Tennessee is allowing 266.9 passing yards per tilt, which is last in the league.
